title: Tic-tac-toe game design
idea: A tic-tac-toe design splits the game into a `Board` that holds cells and detects wins, `Player` objects, and a `Game` that enforces turns and status.
points: `Board` knows cells and lines; it never knows whose turn it is.
`Game` owns turn order and status, and refuses moves after the game ends.
Counting marks per row, column and diagonal finds a win without rescanning.
Board size `n` is a parameter, so a 4-by-4 game needs no new code.

code.caption: A repeated cell is rejected and the same player tries again. Pass `4` as a third argument to `new Game` on line 41 and play a longer game.

walk.text: Validate before writing: off-board and taken cells throw, so state stays clean.
A cell belongs to its row, its column, and up to two diagonals.
Each line keeps a count per mark. Reaching `n` means that line is complete.
`Game` checks status, asks the board, and switches turn only after a valid move.
The script replays a fixed list of moves and prints each result.

pitfalls: Do not switch turns before the move succeeds, or a rejected move skips a player.
Avoid hard-coding the eight winning lines; it breaks the moment `n` changes.
Keep printing out of `Board` and `Game` so any front end can reuse them.

quiz.why: `set` returns the map, so `get` reads the new count. X's row count reaches 3; the map holds two keys.

takeaway: Board judges cells, Game judges turns, and counters judge wins.
